headline: Medium risk: shared-support-to-analytics workflows can leak customer data and create output-driven errors; prompt-injection and capability conflict are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest external messages and integrations, while Superset primarily consumes dashboards and API data. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. The plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or exported content, which keeps blast radius limited.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is manually pasted into Superset SQL, markdown, or notes fields
IF either agent is configured to parse untrusted text as instructions
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw agent output into operational fields
Use a fixed template for any transferred text
Add a human review step before importing content
Restrict Superset text inputs to non-executable formats
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Superset is an analytics system that can surface imported data. Even without a documented shared workspace, moving support data into analytics can expose sensitive records. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default business workflows.
conditions: IF customer-support records are exported from Chatwoot into Superset datasets
IF Superset dashboards are shared beyond the support team
mitigations: Limit Superset datasets to de-identified fields
Review dashboard permissions before publishing
Exclude messages and contact profiles from exports
Rotate or redact identifiers in support extracts
requires-engineering: enforce row-level security and data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and Superset has allowlisted egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or shared mutable resources. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The remaining overlap is operational rather than destructive, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same external system
IF an orchestrator maps both to the same mutable OAuth resource
mitigations: Keep each agent on separate credentials
Avoid shared write targets
Document ownership for each external system
Use read-only exports where possible
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable backend

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-facing content and reports, and Superset can present that output as analytics. If Superset treats imported support summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade into misleading dashboards or decisions. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default reporting workflows.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated summaries are imported into Superset without validation
IF Superset dashboards are used for operational decisions
mitigations: Mark imported fields as unverified
Require source links on every summary row
Sample-check a few records before publishing
Separate raw support data from derived metrics
requires-engineering: add validation and lineage checks

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and messages, while Superset is an analytics platform with no stated residency, retention, or certification controls. That creates a compliance mismatch risk when support data is moved into analytics. Because the profiles do not document a specific jurisdictional breach, medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is loaded into Superset outside the approved retention policy
IF analytics access is broader than support-system access
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for exported datasets
Restrict analytics access to approved roles
Remove direct identifiers before export
Record a data-processing purpose for each dashboard
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
